messages:
Sasha: Heads-up — onboarding run for mithril20b (int4) hit a cluster of OOMs during soak. Patterns look like slow memory reclamation (fragmentation) + a few requests with big max_new_tokens.
Raj: Can you paste the config + a sample stack? Also: what batch sizes and `max_new_tokens` distribution are we seeing?
Sasha: quick logs below — most OOMs at token ~450-520. Many requests spiked max_new_tokens=1024. We defaulted batch_size=4 for this canary.
Elaine: ugh. int4 + large generation windows are classic frag combos. If we can keep max_new_tokens <= 128 for the first rollout, that'd help. Try `prefetch.enabled=false` as a quick experiment?
Sasha: sample config: ```json
{"model":"mithril20b-int4","batch_size":4,"prefetch":true,"max_new_tokens_default":256,"kv_trim_threshold":"auto"}
```
Marcos: preferring `prefetch=false` reduces concurrent resident allocations; also set `kv_trim_threshold=0.6` so the eviction runs earlier.
Tom: Another lever: set per-model `max_new_tokens_policy`: "soft_cap=256, hard_cap=512" so client gets a friendly 256 but we still bound 512 for emergencies.
Elaine: +1 on soft/hard caps. For rollout, canary at 10% traffic with `warmup_slots=2` and `slot_compactor=aggressive` reduced frag on Helios tests.
Sasha: infra-bot reported node snapshots: free pages transiently spike then fail to coalesce. Might need a kernel-level compaction flag or driver-level defrag.
infra-bot: [system] Noted: scheduled low-impact mem-defrag on prod-nodes in 30m window (rolling).
Raj: Also consider changing batching policy to "max_tokens_per_batch" instead of fixed batch_size=4. That keeps token memory bounded when a single request asks for 1k tokens.
Marcos: For immediate mitigation: 1) set `max_new_tokens_default=128` 2) add `per_request_max=512` 3) disable prefetch 4) enable kv_trim=0.6. Deploy these as a canary config and monitor token-failure-rate.
Sasha: I'll push the canary in 10m with those limits. Will post results. Thanks folks :thumbsup:
Tom: If we still see tail OOMs, I'll open a kernel-defrag runbook and schedule a deeper sweep with the CUDA driver team.
Sasha: Update in 15m — canary up, initial traffic looks stable, no OOMs in first 10m. Will keep monitoring for 1h.
Marcos: Nice. After stability, we should run a calibrated quality sweep at max_new_tokens=256 vs 128 to quantify degradation before removing the soft cap.
